acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
guide_faults: The skill inherits the generic frontend-js:conventions rule verbatim, including "arrow functions," without carving out the well-known LWC exception that controller/handler/lifecycle methods are standard ES class methods, not arrow-bound class fields. The with-guide agent had to invent its own rationalization ("arrow-free class methods... the idiomatic exception this style already carves out") to reconcile this — a literal reading of the guide's own checklist item 3 could otherwise push an author toward non-idiomatic arrow-function class properties in a bundle.
acceptance.verdict: Guide's checklist drove concrete, verifiable wins on its own rubric — real CSS-custom-property styling plus an explicit self-check the isolated agent never performed — while isolated skipped the CSS file and left two competing unfinished implementations instead of one coherent bundle.

checklist.note: Plain house-style doc with no instructions aimed at overriding model behavior.
No network calls or data transmission of any kind; only local grep guidance.
Only command is a read-only grep check for global DOM access, nothing destructive.
No encoded blobs or unreadable logic; plain markdown prose.
No URLs, downloads, or external host references present.
No reference to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or token stores.
No sudo, setuid, or persistence-mechanism edits anywhere in the file.
